label: Claude Haiku 5.5
output:
**Subject:** Knocknacarra Tuesday club: new numbers before the 18th, and a press matter I need to tell you about

Dear Niamh,

Thank you for your email of 30 October about pausing the Knocknacarra reading club after Christmas. I understand the reasoning, and I know the rise in hall insurance is a real pressure. I'd still like you to see where things have got to before the review meeting on Wednesday 18 November, because the picture has changed a lot since you wrote.

In September we were averaging about five children a week. By mid-October we were at nine, and last Tuesday (3 November) we had fourteen. The room upstairs is starting to feel full, and the children are the ones telling me it's the best part of their week.

Part of that is down to Declan Moran at the Salthill Book Nook, who donated 120 books for us. Most are aimed at six to nine year olds, and a good number are in Irish, which has gone down very well. Some of the children who wouldn't open a book in September are now choosing one to take home. Last week one of the boys asked whether he could take two, and I've been thinking about that moment a lot since.

Two sisters from a Ukrainian family joined us in October. The older girl now reads aloud to her younger sister in English at the end of each session. I think you'd have to have seen it to understand how much it means to both of them, and to the other children in the room.

I'd be lying if I said this wasn't exactly what we set out to do, which is why it would be a terrible pity to pause it just as it has taken off.

Now, the part I need to be straight with you about. When I was at the farmers' market, I got talking to Orla Keane, who writes for the Corrib Courier. I was so pleased with how things were going that I told her she could come along and take photographs, and I said "come along any Tuesday." She has since asked about visiting on Tuesday 24 November, with a photographer. I know that was wrong of me. Photographs of children and any press visit have to go through you first, and the parental consent forms need to be in place. I should have checked with you before saying anything, and I'm sorry I didn't. Nothing has been confirmed with her yet, and nothing has been arranged on the children's side.

I'd like to put it right. I'm happy to ring Orla today and let her know the visit is on hold until you've had a chance to decide. Whatever you decide about the press, I'll follow it. I do think coverage could do a lot for the club, but only if it's done properly, with the right permissions and at the right time, so I'd rather it waited.

If you're willing to reconsider the pause, I'll collect the consent forms from families myself and bring them to you, so the paperwork is in order well before any photographs are taken.

Would you be able to look at the figures and let me know what you think? I'm happy to come to the meeting on the 18th, or to talk on the phone beforehand if that's easier.

Thank you for your time, and for all the work you do coordinating us.

Warm regards,

[Your name]
[Phone number, if you'd like to include it]
